finding: The derivative-consistent adaptive representation is consistently faster than the analytical provider in the long paired complete-Richards benchmark while preserving the analytical nonlinear path and frozen fidelity gates.
interpretation: The main numerical lesson of F-AHL04 through F-AHL09 is that constitutive approximation must preserve the theta-C derivative relationship. Once that relationship is enforced through a shared interpolant, the table can be both compact and computationally beneficial.
next_action: Cross-material and cross-regime falsification before any production-oriented work.
nonclaims: This is one controlled nonlinear Richards fixture.
This is not a whole-SWAP speedup claim.
